sections.h2: Where is Cass County, Missouri, and how did it start?
sections.html:
Western Missouri holds Cass County, right against the Kansas line and inside the Kansas City metro area. Harrisonville serves as seat, and a slice of Kansas City itself falls within the county. It covers 697 square miles of land. Wikipedia notes that Cass is one of the few counties in the country that borders two counties of the same name in different states, Johnson County in Missouri and Johnson County in Kansas.

The county was organized in 1835 as Van Buren County and renamed in 1849 for U.S. Senator Lewis Cass of Michigan. James Lackey was the first settler on the site of Harrisonville in 1830. The town was platted in 1837 and named for Representative Albert G. Harrison. During the Civil War it was emptied in 1863 when federal forces pushed residents out, and most of the buildings were burned.

The 2020 census counted 107,824 people, of whom 70.3 percent lived in urban areas.

sections.h2: Which cities and school districts are in Cass County?
sections.html:
The cities are Archie, Belton, Cleveland, Creighton, Drexel, East Lynne, Freeman, Garden City, Harrisonville, Lake Annette, Lake Winnebago, Peculiar, Pleasant Hill, Raymore and Strasburg, plus parts of Kansas City and Lee's Summit. The county's Helpful Numbers page gives a phone line for most of them, such as 816-380-8900 for Harrisonville and 816-331-7916 for Raymore.

Wikipedia lists these full K-12 districts that serve the county:

  • Harrisonville R-IX, Belton, Raymore-Peculiar R-II and Pleasant Hill R-III
  • Archie R-V, Drexel R-IV, Holden R-III and Kingsville R-I
  • Lee's Summit R-VII, Lone Jack C-VI, Sherwood Cass R-VIII and Midway R-I

Because the county runs from the Kansas City suburbs south to Drexel and Archie, two houses with the same assessed value can carry very different levies. Check the district on the tax bill, not only the mailing address.

sections.h2: How does Cass County compare on housing and income?
sections.html:
Cass is the fastest growing and highest income county of the four Missouri counties in this comparison. The Census QuickFacts table below shows the numbers.

Owners live in 75.6 percent of homes, the poverty rate is 7.0 percent, and workers average a 28.0 minute commute, the longest of the four. Retail sales reached $2.0 billion in 2022. With 487 permits issued in 2025, new subdivisions compete with resale houses in Belton, Raymore and Peculiar, and a seller with an older house in Harrisonville or Pleasant Hill faces buyers who can choose between both.

sections.h2: Who collects and assesses property tax in Cass County?
sections.html:
The Collector and the Assessor are neighbors on Cantrell Road in Harrisonville.

  • Collector Chris Molendorp, 2725 Cantrell Road, 816-380-8377, collector@casscounty.com, with weekday counter service from eight until half past four
  • Assessor Roger Raffety, 2733 Cantrell Road, 816-380-8400. He joined the office as an appraiser in 2005 and was appointed Assessor in January 2019.
  • County Clerk Kathy Lambertz, Historic Courthouse, 102 E. Wall Street, who handles the secretarial work for the Board of Equalization.

The Collector's drop box is at Annex 1, 201 W. Wall Street, and a payment placed in it before midnight on December 31 is timely. The county's FAQ stresses that the Treasurer's office, held by Steve Cheslik, does not take property tax. Recorder of Deeds Mike Medsker handles deeds. The portal at casscountycollector.org lets you search tax records and print receipts.

sections.h2: What is the Cass County due date, and what do late payments cost?
sections.html:
Real estate tax is due on receipt of the bill and no later than December 31. The Collector mails bills during November, and a U.S. postmark decides whether a mailed payment is on time, because the county does not accept its own metered date. If no bill arrives by the end of November, call 816-380-8377.

Taxes not paid in full by December 31 accrue penalties and fees that can reach 25 percent in the first year of delinquency, according to the Collector's General Information page. Missing a bill does not excuse the debt. A lien follows the property, so when ownership changes the new owner is liable for any unpaid tax.

An owner who sells on or after October 1 may have the bill mailed to the old address, because it follows the file as of the print date. Sellers who receive a bill for a house they sold should send the Collector the new owner's name and address, and buyers who have not received a bill by December 10 should call.

sections.h2: How is a Cass County tax bill calculated?
sections.html:
The bill comes from the assessed value and the combined levies of the taxing districts where the parcel sits. The Collector's example is $9,500 of assessed value divided by 100 and multiplied by a 5.66 percent rate, which gives $537.70.

  • Residential property is assessed at 19 percent of market value.
  • Commercial property is assessed at 32 percent.
  • Agricultural property is assessed at 12 percent.

By the county's own example, a $50,000 residence is assessed at $9,500. Real estate is reassessed in odd-numbered years, and new construction is added to the value when it is finished. An increase in assessed value does not always raise the bill, because levies are set in September and can fall. Ask the Assessor at 816-380-8400 whether the county has adopted a homestead credit under RSMo 137.1050 before you assume one applies to the house you are selling.

sections.h2: What are the steps to appeal in Cass County?
sections.html:
You have three steps, and the county tells owners that saying taxes are too high is not relevant testimony. The value is the question, so bring photographs, a recent sale of your property or an appraiser's statement.

  1. Meet informally with the Assessor's staff.
  2. File the Board of Equalization appeal form with the Assessor. For 2026 it had to be postmarked by July 13.
  3. Appeal to the State Tax Commission by September 30, 2026 or 30 days after the Board's final action, whichever is later.

Both 2026 dates have passed, so the next appeal cycle follows the 2027 reassessment. The Board of Equalization is appointed by the County Commission, and the County Clerk's office keeps its records. State law behind these steps is in RSMo 138.430, and the July cutoff is in RSMo 137.275.

sections.h2: When is the Cass County tax certificate sale?
sections.html:
It is held every year on the fourth Monday in August at 10 a.m. at the courthouse, 102 E. Wall Street in Harrisonville, and the 2026 sale date of August 24 has passed. The next falls in August 2027. The Collector says property is subject to sale if its real estate taxes remain unpaid after March 1 of the following year. State law sets the sale day at the fourth Monday in RSMo 140.150 and requires the Collector to mail notices to the record owner first.

A parcel on the list can still be cleared by paying the delinquent tax, penalty, interest and costs before the sale. The Collector's site has a bidders section for people who want to register. For a seller, the sale list is a deadline: clear the balance at closing and the parcel comes off.

sections.h2: What happens to Cass County property tax at closing?
sections.html:
The county explains that taxes are generally prorated between buyer and seller, with the buyer credited for the days the seller owned the house in the tax year. No money is paid to the Collector at the time of sale, and the new owner pays the whole bill by December 31. If a mortgage company escrows the tax, it should be told of any payoff, and the lender normally returns any escrow balance or credits it to the loan.

Recording is quick. The Cass County Recorder's FAQ says real estate recordings are turned around the same day or within 24 hours, excluding weekends and holidays. A recorded deed does not show the sale price, and the office does not call with closing information or do lien searches, so ask the title company, since liens can also sit with the courts or the Collector.

Cash Home Buyers works with Cass County owners who have unpaid tax, a tenant, an inherited house or deferred repairs, and can give a written offer after seeing the property.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Cass County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Collector at 2725 Cantrell Road, Harrisonville, on weekdays. A drop box at 201 W. Wall Street is timely until midnight December 31, and the Collector's portal at casscountycollector.org shows bills.

faqs.q: How big is the Cass County late penalty?
faqs.a: Penalties and fees can reach 25 percent in the first year of delinquency, and they begin after December 31. A mailed payment is on time only if the U.S. postmark is December 31 or earlier.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or seller pay Cass County property tax at closing?
faqs.a: Taxes are generally prorated, with the buyer credited for the part of the year the seller owned the house. No tax is paid to the Collector at closing, and the buyer pays the full bill by December 31.

faqs.q: When is the Cass County tax certificate sale?
faqs.a: On the fourth Monday in August at 10 a.m. at the courthouse, 102 E. Wall Street, Harrisonville. Property is exposed to sale if its real estate taxes stay unpaid after March 1 of the following year.

faqs.q: How do I contest my Cass County assessed value?
faqs.a: Talk to the Assessor at 816-380-8400 first, then file the Board of Equalization form with the Assessor by its July postmark date. A further appeal goes to the State Tax Commission by September 30 or 30 days after the Board's decision.
